title: What a Fresh 48-Month Inspection Really Means
hook: The calendar doesn't care how much you flew.
body:
A lot of major inspections on business jets are calendar-driven, not hours-driven. The 48-month is one of the big ones — it comes due whether the aircraft flew 400 hours or 40. That means real downtime at a shop, on top of the invoice.

When a listing shows a fresh 48-month, the next owner is inheriting a clean slate instead of a bill — roughly four years before that clock resets again.

The purchase price is only half the number. Where the aircraft sits in its inspection cycle is the other half. Two similar aircraft at similar asking prices can be very far apart in true cost depending on what's due.

Ask where an aircraft sits in its maintenance cycle before you compare prices. It's one of the first things we look at for a client.
